Add glyphs & languages
English letters
Adds an English tab to design A–Z and a–z (with an uppercase/lowercase switch). Accent-supporting letters can carry accents (á, é, ñ, ç…). Template: PDF · PNG
Specialized letters
Adds a Specialized letters tab with the wide letterforms (wide alef, dalet, he, kaf, lamed, final mem, resh, tav) — auto-composed from your traced letters, each with a Width slider that adds space & stretches.
Yiddish
Adds a Yiddish tab: pasekh/komets alef (אַ אָ), the rafe letters (בֿ כֿ פֿ), and the digraphs tsvey vovn / vov-yud / tsvey yudn (װ ױ ײ) — all composed from your traced letters.
Ladino
Adds a Ladino (Judeo-Spanish) tab: the rafe / varika letters (בֿ גֿ דֿ זֿ טֿ פֿ קֿ) plus שׁ / שׂ — composed from your traced letters.
Custom glyphs
Adds a Custom glyphs tab (after Punctuation) where you can define glyphs at any Unicode code point — a main letter or a nikkud mark. Tip: for brand-new shapes use the Private-Use range U+E000–U+F8FF so they don't collide with standard characters.
Input mode
SVG uploading
Upload SVG files instead of images — vector paths become the glyph outlines directly, with no tracing. In this mode the upload zones accept SVG only. SVG Upload Guide →

Frequently Asked Questions
Is the Hebrew Font Maker free?

Yes. The Hebrew Font Maker is completely free — make and download as many Hebrew fonts as you like, with no account or sign-up.

How do I make my own Hebrew font?

Upload or scan a picture of each Hebrew letter, trace it into an outline, place the nikkud and trop anchors, then export a real font you can install.

Can I make free Hebrew fonts with nikkud and trop?

Yes. The free Hebrew Font Maker positions nikkud (vowels) and cantillation (trop) automatically using OpenType mark positioning.

What font formats can I export?

TrueType (TTF), WOFF2 for the web, and editable UFO source — each with a license you choose (CC0, OFL, MIT, or All Rights Reserved).

Do I need to install any software?

No. The Hebrew Font Maker runs entirely in your browser; the font engine loads only when you export.

How do I install a Hebrew font on Windows, Mac, or Google Docs?

On Windows, double-click the downloaded .ttf file and choose Install. On Mac, double-click it and click Install Font in Font Book. Google Docs only uses fonts from its own catalog and cannot load a local font, so use a desktop word processor such as Word, Pages, or LibreOffice, or upload the file to a design tool like Canva instead.

Are fonts I make here free to use commercially?

That depends on the license you pick when you export. CC0 places the font in the public domain — free for any use, including commercial, with no attribution required. OFL and MIT are also free for commercial use under their terms. All Rights Reserved keeps the font yours to license as you wish. You own what you create; IvritSuite claims no rights to your fonts.

Do the fonts include nikkud (vowels) and cantillation (trop)?

Yes. As you build each letter you can anchor its nikkud and trop marks, and the exported font uses OpenType GPOS mark positioning so the marks land in the right place automatically as you type. You can also make a letters-only font and skip the marks.

About
A free, experimental IvritSuite tool. Builds real fonts entirely client-side (the font engine loads on first export), with GPOS mark positioning for nikkud (mark-to-base) and cantillation/trop (mark-to-mark). Exports TrueType (TTF), WOFF2 and editable UFO source.

Enter a font name and author to continue.

Apply this alignment to other letters

Copies the current letter's position & scale (its image transform — not its traced outline) onto the letters you pick, overwriting their current alignment. You can undo it.

Apply this positioning to other letters

Copies where this letter's nikkud & trop marks sit (the anchor positions) onto the letters you pick, overwriting theirs. You can undo it.

On: copies the vertical positions and keeps each mark centered on the target letter's own width (best when letters differ in width). Off: copies the exact X positions too.

Copy outline from another letter

Drops a letter's traced outline into this letter as a starting point — then reshape it (e.g. copy Tav and delete the toe to make Het, He or Resh) with ✎ Edit points. The current letter's width & spacing stay as they are. You can undo it.

New kern class

A named group of letters you can kern as a unit (e.g. all wide-top letters). Use it on either side of a pair; editing the class later updates every pair that uses it.
